rules.name: Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI)
rules.desc: Students must take the Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI) two quarters prior to degree conferral. Students should contact the Stanford Language Center to arrange assessment.

rules.name: Required Coursework
rules.desc:
• Coursework within the department. Additional GERMAN courses at the 100- or 200- level.

• Language coursework. All GERLANG courses from the Language Center may be counted.

• Bing Overseas Program. Courses taken at the Bing Overseas Studies in Berlin program with prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Education as Self-Fashioning (ESF), Structured Liberal Education (SLE), relevant IntroSems or COLLEGE courses may contribute a maximum of ten units.

• Subject to approval by the Director of Undergraduate Studies, courses from other fields may count if they contribute to the student’s language skills, the ability to interpret literature and other cultural material, or the capacity to analyze societies.
This course introduces students to writing as a process and is designed to combine students’ specific disciplinary interest with a focus on German and the German-speaking world.

rules.name: German and Philosophy Subplan Capstone Experience

children.name: Philosophy and Literature Capstone Seminar
children.desc: Students must take one course designated as a philosophy and literature capstone with the approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies and the Faculty Advisor for Philosophy.

children.name: Honors Thesis
children.desc:
Students majoring in any DLCL department (i.e., Comparative Literature, French and Italian, German Studies, Iberian and Latin American Cultures, and Slavic Languages and Literatures) who have an overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.3 or above and who maintain a 3.5 (GPA) in their major courses, are eligible to participate in the DLCL’s honors program.
See the Honors webpage for more information.
Program Requirements
To earn honors, students must complete a minimum of 9 units (3 units per quarter), submit a thesis, and present at the Honors Colloquium at the end of their senior year.

children.name: 5,000-word Topic Paper
children.desc:
The student will write a 5,000-word paper on a topic of their choosing, serving as the culmination of their work in the field.
To write the paper, students must enroll in a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member (or affiliate) in the Philosophy and Literature Focal Group. The paper must involve philosophy and literature, and the faculty member must approve the topic by the add/drop deadline.

rules.name: German and Philosophy Subplan Policies:
rules.desc:
• The German and Philosophy subplan requires 65 units. Students interested in this option should review the Philosophy and Literature website.

• Up to 10 units taken in the Philosophy Department may be taken CR/NC or S/NC; the remainder must be taken for a letter grade.

• Substitutions, including transfer credit, are generally not permitted.

• Units devoted to meeting the department’s language requirement are not counted toward the 65-unit requirement.

rules.name: Aesthetics, Ethics, Political Philosophy
rules.desc: Substitutions and transfer credits are generally not permitted for the PHIL 170 series class.

rules.name: Language, Mind Metaphysics, and Epistemology
rules.desc: Substitutions and transfer credits are generally not permitted for the PHIL 180 series classes.

rules.name: History of Philosophy
rules.desc: At least one course in the history of philosophy, numbered above PHIL 100.

rules.name: Elective Courses
rules.desc: Two additional elective courses of special relevance to the study of philosophy and literature. Students must consult with the Chair of Undergraduate Studies in German Studies.
